sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference (time-based media criteria)
sources.version_commit: WCAG 2.2; current Quick Reference page observed 2026-10-09 (page is living guidance)
sources.locator: Guideline 1.2; SC 1.2.2, 1.2.3; sufficient techniques and failure notes
sources.evidence_note: Synchronized-media captions are SC 1.2.2 Level A; SC 1.2.3 allows audio description or a time-based media alternative for prerecorded synchronized media.

sources.title: Understanding SC 1.2.2: Captions (Prerecorded)
sources.version_commit: WCAG 2.2 Understanding document; informative explanation, page accessed 2026-10-09
sources.locator: Definition of captions; note describing non-dialogue audio and speaker identification
sources.evidence_note: The WAI explanation describes captions as synchronized equivalents for speech and meaningful non-speech audio; it says captions include information such as effects, music, laughter, and speaker identification.

sources.title: WHATWG HTML Standard — Media elements / track element
sources.version_commit: WHATWG HTML Living Standard; page accessed 2026-10-09, mutable standard
sources.locator: Track element; text-track kinds; kind, label, srclang and default attributes
sources.evidence_note: HTML defines text-track kinds including captions, subtitles, chapters, descriptions and metadata; the track label is used by user agents and srclang identifies the track language. At most one caption/subtitle track child may be marked default.

sources.title: WebVTT: The Web Video Text Tracks Format
sources.version_commit: W3C WebVTT Candidate Recommendation Draft as served 2026-10-09; publication history on W3C WebVTT series page
sources.locator: §4.1 WebVTT cue timings; cue start/end constraints and ordering
sources.evidence_note: Cue starts are nondecreasing, each end is after its own start, cue blocks are ordered by start time, and distinct cues may overlap.

sources.title: Able Player official documentation and README
sources.version_commit: README and project docs on mutable main; package.json reports version 5.0.0; no main-branch commit SHA exposed in the inspected page
sources.locator: Feature list; Closed Captions; Interactive Transcript; Video Transcript Sorter; YouTube/Vimeo limitations; preferences
observed_operations: web search retrieved official repository and project site
sources.evidence_note: Docs describe keyboard and screen-reader controls, user caption preferences, WebVTT-only caption tracks, generated/manual transcripts, VTS synchronization aid, and reduced functionality with remote-hosted captions alone.

sources.title: Able Player v5.0.0 release
sources.version_commit: v5.0.0, short commit 8d235f9, released 2026-06-21; release page showed it as latest at access
sources.locator: v5.0.0 release notes and release list

sources.evidence_note: The release page identifies v5.0.0/8d235f9 and notes fixes including Vimeo error handling, playlist navigation, volume display, seekbar width, and language handling.

sources.title: Able Player issue #775 — develop YouTube regression report
sources.version_commit: Issue #775; report references develop regressions originating at 834d003, 2d4a1c2, and 05e9a22; issue page observed 2026-10-09
sources.locator: Issue body lines 130-228; issue description, tested-version caveat, regressions, reported repro and demo-test results
sources.evidence_note: Reporter says a freshly built develop version broke YouTube and 17/60 demos, while released 5.0.0 did not; checked-in stale build masked regressions. Results are attributed to the issue reporter, not an independent test here.

sources.evidence_note: Maintainer merged one commit into develop; the page reports seven checks passed. The inspected release list does not show a later tagged release containing this fix.

sources.title: Subtitle Edit 5 official documentation: FAQ, overview, audio visualizer, STT and formats
sources.url: https://github.com/SubtitleEdit/subtitleedit/tree/main/docs (key pages: docs/faq.md, docs/overview.md, docs/features/audio-visualizer.md, docs/features/speech-to-text.md, docs/reference/supported-formats.md)

sources.title: Amara official support: captions/translations and subtitle upload
sources.version_commit: Official support documentation; create-captions article modified 2026-06-09; accessed 2026-10-09
sources.locator: Create captions and translations; team requests; language selection; upload/export and existing-language replacement details
sources.evidence_note: Help describes collaborative language editing and team workflow; uploaded tracks can replace an existing version, and some upload workflows mark a track complete.

sources.title: YouTube Help — Edit or remove captions
sources.locator: Edit captions; edit caption timing; download and edit caption files
observed_operations: web search retrieved official help page
sources.evidence_note: YouTube Studio permits text/timestamp changes, a duplicate-and-edit route for automatic captions, publishing, download, external editing, and re-upload.

sources.title: W3C TTML profile comparison overview
sources.version_commit: W3C overview page; page is old and accessed 2026-10-09; used only for format distinction, not current product support
sources.evidence_note: The page contrasts text-based WebVTT with XML-based TTML and emphasizes profile/delivery distinctions. Current HTML/WebVTT specifications and chosen distributor requirements should govern implementation.

sources.title: DCMP Captioning Key
sources.locator: Captioning Key overview; speaker identification; non-speech sound and music; language mechanics
sources.evidence_note: DCMP describes captions as including dialogue plus speaker identification, sound effects and music description; it is an editorial resource, not the WCAG normative text.

sources.title: 17 U.S.C. §106, U.S. Code (2023 edition)
sources.version_commit: United States Code 2023 edition, §106; jurisdiction-specific statutory source
sources.locator: §106(2), exclusive right to prepare derivative works; §101 definition reference for translation in the official source notes
observed_operations: web search retrieved official GovInfo page
sources.evidence_note: U.S. law provides a jurisdiction-specific example: §106 lists preparation of derivative works among exclusive rights, subject to statutory limitations and exceptions; the related statutory definition names translation. This is not a global legal conclusion.
